To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the blockchain protocol can be deconstructed into its basic functionalities, and that the throughput, confirmation latency, confirmation reliability and eventual total ordering of a blockchain protocol can be systematically improved towards their physical limits by scaling up the corresponding functionalities.
a blockchain protocol can approach the physical limits of security, throughput, latency and reliability.

the throughput of a proof-of-work protocol can be scaled up to the capacity of the underlying network, the confirmation latency of an honest transaction can be reduced to the propagation delay of the network, and the confirmation reliability can be improved to exponentially small in the network bandwidth-delay product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
three main questions: What is a blockchain? Why is the blockchain so slow? How to make the blockchain fast?

the following questions: (i) What are the physical limits of a blockchain protocol? (ii) What is the optimal design of a blockchain protocol that achieves these limits? (iii) Can we design a blockchain protocol that approaches these physical limits?

the following fundamental questions. How to achieve optimal performance for a blockchain protocol? What are the physical limits of a blockchain? How can a blockchain protocol be designed to approach these physical limits?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have deconstructed the blockchain to approach its physical limits.
the blockchain is an elegant solution to the Byzantine Generals Problem, and that its performance is limited by the physical properties of the network.
the blockchain protocol is a distributed system that is secure, efficient and scalable, and that it is a viable alternative to existing payment systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a blockchain is an information dissemination system that can achieve optimal throughput, latency and reliability in the presence of an adversary with up to half of the hashing power.

the throughput, latency and reliability of a blockchain system can all be improved by orders of magnitude, and that the security of a blockchain protocol can be improved to be resilient to a large fraction of adversarial hashing power, by carefully deconstructing the existing blockchain design and scaling up each of its functionalities.
we can build a blockchain system that achieves optimal performance, and is as secure as the network itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the blockchain can be made as efficient as possible, without compromising its security, and that the design of efficient blockchain protocols is possible without relying on any assumptions on the adversary.
it is possible to design a blockchain protocol that can operate near the physical limits of a network.
the physical limits of the network can be used to design a secure blockchain protocol with optimal performance.
